name: Calcutta women’s early commercial recordings
description: Women performers including Soshi Mukhi and Gauharjan recorded songs in Calcutta for the Gramophone and Typewriter Company.

date.label: November 1902
date.basis: The cited historical account provides this date.

events.statement: Soshi Mukhi and Gauharjan sang during Gaisberg’s November 1902 recording sessions in Calcutta.

evidence.supports: Describes Indian-language records made in England in 1899 and Gaisberg’s November 1902 Calcutta sessions involving Soshi Mukhi and Gauharjan; notes high early playback costs.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped episode established in these sources; not a global priority claim.

caveats: The archival report also notes Indian-language recordings made in England in 1899; these are not claimed as the first Indian recordings anywhere. Its report is a retrospective project account. High early costs constrained access; a recording session does not prove a release date, sales volume or who could afford records.

research.note: Independent review checked the date, location and participants against the British Library project report; performers are credited as contributors.
